picks.d: San Francisco is ground zero for the biggest Pokémon event of the year — world-class competitors duking it out at Moscone while fans shop the exclusive pop-up Pokémon Center store and catch panels all weekend. Even if you're not competing, the free activations around the venue make it worth swinging by. Gotta catch at least one.

picks.t: Tori Amos — In Times of Dragons Tour
picks.d: One of rock's most singular voices plays the Greek Theatre in Berkeley with Bartees Strange opening — an absolutely perfect late-summer pairing at one of the Bay's most magical outdoor venues. Tori's classically-influenced art rock hits different under the stars. Grab a pre-show picnic and arrive early.

Brand new and completely free: Leland Avenue transforms into a full-on block party with food vendors, live music, street dancing, and local makers for the very first time. This is the kind of neighborhood moment SF does best — scrappy, real, and genuinely fun. Be part of the first one ever.

The fifth annual Bon Odori celebration takes over the SF Botanical Gardens Fountain Plaza in Golden Gate Park for an afternoon of Japanese folk dancing, food, and community. Free for SF residents and an absolutely gorgeous setting for a Sunday. This one always sells the vibe hard.

picks.t: Treasures of the Pharaohs — de Young Museum
picks.d: SF is the first US city to host this blockbuster exhibition — 130 objects spanning 3,000 years of Egyptian history, including US debuts from the newly excavated Golden City near Luxor. Think of it as Pompeii but make it ancient Egypt. Timed entry is $40 and absolutely worth every penny.

The Castro throws a free afternoon party on Noe between Market and Beaver — LGBTQ+ art, drag performances, and the kind of warm neighborhood energy that makes this city feel like home. Zero cost, maximum good time. Show up, wander, stay longer than you planned.

One of SF's most respected underground promoters stacks a genuinely killer lineup at Club Six — TAYHANA headlining is a big deal, and this crew doesn't do mid. If you care about electronic music done right in a safe, inclusive space, this is your Friday night. Check ra.co for tickets.

picks.t: Wax + DJ Hoppa (w/ K.A.A.N. & Intuition & Equalibrum)
picks.d: Four deep hip-hop acts on one bill at The Independent — Wax's introspective wordplay is the kind of thing that makes you stop mid-drink and think 'wait, that was actually incredible.' Intimate venue, serious rap, Friday night energy. This is a great one for hip-hop heads.

The last Friday of the month means Critical Mass rolls out from Embarcadero Plaza — no sign-up, no route announced in advance, just hundreds of cyclists taking back the streets together. A beloved SF institution that's equal parts protest, party, and pure joy. Bring your bike and show up.

Last home stand before the long weekend ends — catch the Giants at Oracle Park with the Bay as your backdrop. Saturday is a doubleheader which means double the baseball for your buck. Late-summer Oracle Park on a warm evening is one of SF's great pleasures.

Philly indie rock that hits hard and feels harder — Sweet Pill's live show is emotionally charged in the best way, and August Hall is a great room for it. Tickets start around $23 which makes this an easy yes. Great opener to a packed Friday night.

The team behind Lazy Bear and True Laurel just opened their most ambitious project yet — a French-leaning seafood playground with oysters, frites, shellfish towers, and multiple distinct rooms to match your mood. This is the hottest new reservation in the city right now, full stop.

The legendary Punch Line hosts Derrick Stroup for a full weekend run — this is the room where Dave Chappelle and Chris Rock cut their teeth, and it still delivers. Multiple shows Friday and Saturday means you can actually get a ticket. From $35 and a seriously fun night.

picks.t: SF Symphony: Infinity Saga Concert Experience
picks.d: The SF Symphony plays the full Marvel Cinematic Universe score live — conducted by Anthony Parnther at Davies Symphony Hall, which means the acoustics are going to make 'Avengers: Endgame' feel like a religious experience. A genuinely great date-night or family pick to close out the week.

ongoing.t: Treasures of the Pharaohs — de Young Museum
ongoing.d: 130 objects, 3,000 years of Egypt — SF is the only US stop. Through Jan 31, 2027.
Immersive, hands-on space science at Pier 15. Through September 13.

ongoing.t: Lala Rukh: Subh-e-Umeed — Asian Art Museum
ongoing.d: First West Coast showing of Pakistani artist Lala Rukh's sonic archive. Through September 7.
Major retrospective of the legendary Mexican photographer, open through the fall.
Beautiful evening hours at the historic gardens. Through September 3.

ongoing.t: Union Square Dances — Free Outdoor Dance Party
ongoing.d: Free rotating dance styles every Friday 5–8pm through October 16.

new.name: JouJou
new.d: Lazy Bear's David Barzelay opens a playful French seafood spot — oysters, frites, shellfish towers, multiple vibe-matched rooms from raw bar to banquette.

new.name: Rose Pizzeria
new.d: Berkeley's beloved natural-wine-and-snappy-crust pizzeria opens its SF outpost in the old Village Pizzeria space on Clement.

new.name: The DeLuxe
new.d: The legendary Club Deluxe is back as The DeLuxe — better sound system, classic cocktails, and daily live music across every genre.

new.name: Mess Hall Food Hall
new.d: Huge new all-day food hall in the Presidio with seafood, burgers, Korean, sandwiches, a full bar, and grab-and-go for Tunnel Tops picnics.

new.name: Kissaten Hifi / Kissakeko
new.d: Two new audio-obsessed drinking spots: one spins 1950s jazz over banana cue lattes, the other pours sake with a jazz soundtrack in Nob Hill.

classic.name: Bix
classic.d: Old-school SF glamour — a supper club feel with serious cocktails and crowd-watching that never goes out of style.

classic.name: Good Mong Kok Bakery
classic.d: Cash only, line out the door, dim sum so good it'll ruin you for everywhere else. Classic SF ritual.

classic.name: Swan Oyster Depot
classic.d: Counter seats, chilled Anchor Steam, impossibly fresh dungeness crab. Get there early — the line is the point.

classic.name: La Taqueria
classic.d: The platonic ideal of the SF burrito — no rice, all flavor. A pilgrimage every visitor must make.

classic.name: Cotogna
classic.d: Michael Tusk's rustic Italian is still the best wood-fired dinner in the city — handmade pasta, rotisserie meats, neighborhood warmth.

classic.name: Tartine Manufactory
classic.d: The loaves that launched a thousand bakeries. Saturday morning sourdough at Tartine is a sacred SF experience.

bars.name: The DeLuxe
bars.d: Reborn jazz institution with daily live music and serious cocktails — the Haight needed this back.

bars.name: Kissakeko
bars.d: Tiny, beautiful, jazz-soundtracked sake bar — the coolest low-key spot to open in SF this year.

bars.name: JouJou Bar
bars.d: Pop into the main bar at JouJou for a glass of Champagne and oysters without the full dinner commitment.

bars.name: Blackbird
bars.d: The Castro's anchor cocktail bar — well-made drinks, great people-watching, consistently excellent vibe.

bars.name: Zeitgeist
bars.d: A massive, sunny beer garden in the Mission that's been SF's great outdoor dive forever. Cash, cold beers, no pretense.

bars.name: Vesuvio Café
bars.d: The legendary Beat-era bar next to City Lights — still serving, still pouring, still full of stories.

bars.name: Ordinaire
bars.d: Natural wine, zero attitude, and a rotating list that actually surprises you — perfect pre-symphony stop near Davies.

bars.name: The View at Marriott Marquis
bars.d: Unbeatable 39th-floor panoramic SF views — go at sunset and thank us later.

games.detail: Regular season home stand — waterfront baseball with the Bay as a backdrop
Saturday doubleheader — two games for the price of one, stock up on garlic fries

sports.note: No confirmed Giants home games Aug 30–Sep 3. Next home series begins Sept 7.

games.detail: Valkyries are on the road and heading into the FIBA Women's World Cup break (Sept 4–13). Catch them on TV — next home game is Sept 18 vs. Portland.

sports.note: Chase Center's next confirmed major event after ZAYN cancellation: check the venue directly for any additions.

concerts.t: Tori Amos — In Times of Dragons Tour
concerts.d: A genuine bucket-list show — Tori Amos at the open-air Greek Theatre in Berkeley with Bartees Strange opening is exactly the late-summer concert pairing dreams are made of. Her emotionally complex, classically-inflected art rock rewards deep listening, and this amphitheater rewards showing up. Don't overthink it, just go.

concerts.t: Wax + DJ Hoppa (w/ K.A.A.N. & Intuition & Equalibrum)
concerts.d: Four credible underground hip-hop acts sharing one intimate stage at The Independent — this is the kind of stacked bill that only works in smaller rooms where the lyricists can actually breathe. Wax in particular is a masterclass in wordplay. Show up for K.A.A.N. and stay for all of it.

Philadelphia's Sweet Pill brings their US Tour 2026 to August Hall — emotionally charged indie rock that earns every feeling it puts you through. Tickets from $23 average around $59 which is genuinely fair for what you get. A great Friday night opener before the weekend gets louder.

Emerging indie-pop artist Brenn! takes The Independent on Saturday night — genre-blending and fresh, this is the kind of show you catch before everyone else does and feel smug about it later. The Divisadero corridor is the right neighborhood energy for a Saturday.

Chicago pop-punk legends since the late '80s — if you grew up on fast, melodic punk with hooks that don't quit, Screeching Weasel at August Hall on a Tuesday is the exact chaos your week needs. Their catalog is deep and their fans are devoted.

concerts.t: SF Symphony: Marvel Infinity Saga Concert Experience
concerts.d: The SF Symphony plays the complete MCU score live at Davies Symphony Hall — conducted by Anthony Parnther in one of the best-sounding rooms in America. Whether you're a Marvel devotee or just love a full orchestra doing something unexpected, this is a legitimately great night out.

A legendary SF soul/funk/jazz crossover act at the Castro Theatre — if you want a grown-up dance night with a live band instead of a DJ, this is it. The Castro Theatre itself is worth the price of admission.

One of the Bay's most respected underground electronic promoters brings TAYHANA to Club Six — a genuinely exciting booking in a safe, no-nonsense space. mrs. worldwide and NATHALIA round out a bill that rewards staying until the end. This is what SF underground looks like at its best.

concertsOngoing.d: Opening Gala with Hilary Hahn and conductor Giancarlo Guerrero lands September 24 — tickets on sale now.

concertsOngoing.t: Soccer Mommy (Solo) — The Flannel and the Fury 2026
concertsOngoing.d: Greek Theatre Berkeley, Wednesday September 9. Doors 5pm, show 6pm — just outside this week but worth booking now.

concertsOngoing.t: Peter Pan Goes Wrong — SF Playhouse
concertsOngoing.d: Opens September 26 for a full run through November — the 2026/27 season opener, tickets from ~$100.

singles.d: Eight to twelve local singles, one fun structured evening at Blackbird in the Castro — this format actually works because everyone's there for the same reason and there's zero awkward ambiguity. Age brackets run from 24–38 up through 36–48 so you're matched with your actual people. Search Eventbrite for the live session closest to your preferred night this week.

singles.t: Lock & Key Singles Mixer — Bay Area
singles.d: Women get keys, men get locks, everyone circulates trying to find their match — it sounds cheesy until you're three matches in and laughing with a stranger. These trademarked mixers run across 100+ cities and the Bay Area chapter keeps a solid rotating calendar. Great low-pressure format for people who hate standing around at a regular bar hoping someone talks to them.

singles.t: Visitacion Valley Night Market — Block Party Vibes
singles.d: Free community events are genuinely underrated as meet-cute venues — everyone's relaxed, there's no cover charge awkwardness, and live music plus street dancing gives you something to talk about instantly. This is the inaugural edition which means the crowd is curious and open. Leland Avenue between Bayshore and Peabody.

A free afternoon block party with drag shows, art, and the Castro's signature warmth — the perfect low-stakes Saturday afternoon option that naturally flows into dinner or drinks plans if things go well. Noe between Market and Beaver, noon to 5pm, zero cost to show up.

singles.t: Volo Sports — Coed Volleyball & Pickleball (Sept League)
singles.d: Social sports leagues are one of the best-kept secrets for meeting people in SF — everyone's trying, everyone's laughing, and postgame drinks are basically mandatory. Volo runs intermediate 6v6 coed volleyball at John O'Connell in the Mission on Thursdays and a pickleball tournament at The Crossing at East Cut on Sundays. Sign up now for the September season.

singles.w: Multiple days weekly · Various SF routes
singles.d: The SF Front Runners are the founding chapter of a worldwide LGBTQIA+ running and walking club — welcoming to everyone, all paces, and the post-run hangout is genuinely the point. Run Club SF also offers multiple social group runs weekly that end with drinks. Zero cost, all levels, instant community.

singlesOngoing.t: Union Square Dances — Free Outdoor Dance Party
singlesOngoing.d: Free rotating dance styles with instructors every Friday 5–8pm through October 16 — an easy, no-pressure recurring social event.
Multiple group runs weekly at all levels across SF neighborhoods — social, free, and ends with drinks.
Real-time map of SF club nights updated daily — the easiest way to find where the party actually is any given night.

date.title: Block Party to Bay Views
date.tagline: Castro afternoon energy meets waterfront golden hour — zero dollars, maximum vibe.

steps.title: Castro Carnival Block Party
steps.detail: Start at the free Castro Carnival Block Party on Noe between Market and Beaver — drag shows, art, neighborhood warmth, and built-in conversation starters everywhere you look.

steps.title: Walk to Corona Heights Park
steps.detail: Stroll up to Corona Heights for sweeping 360° views of the city — low-key, slightly secret, and way more romantic than it has any right to be.

steps.title: Union Square Dances
steps.detail: Catch the tail end of the free Union Square Dances — rotating styles, outdoor energy, and a very easy way to be playful together without any pressure.

steps.title: Zeitgeist Beer Garden
steps.detail: Wind down with cold beers at Zeitgeist's massive Mission beer garden. Cash only, no pretense, great outdoor people-watching to close the night.

date.title: Exploratorium to Greyboy Allstars
date.tagline: Hands-on science meets live funk — curious minds, great music, perfect Saturday.

steps.title: Life in Space at the Exploratorium
steps.detail: Spend the morning at the Exploratorium's Life in Space exhibition at Pier 15 — immersive, playful, and genuinely fascinating. Tickets required but worth every cent.

steps.title: Ferry Building Lunch
steps.detail: Walk the Embarcadero to the Ferry Building for lunch — oysters at Hog Island or a slow browse through the market stalls. Waterfront tables if you can grab them.

steps.title: Drinks at The DeLuxe
steps.detail: Head to the newly reopened DeLuxe in the Haight for pre-show cocktails with live music — it's a full evening before the main event even starts.

steps.title: Greyboy Allstars at the Castro Theatre
steps.detail: Catch the Greyboy Allstars at the beautiful Castro Theatre — live soul, funk, and jazz in one of SF's most iconic rooms. A genuinely memorable night.

date.title: Pharaohs & Tori Amos
date.tagline: Ancient Egypt meets art rock legend — the kind of Saturday you actually remember.

steps.title: Treasures of the Pharaohs — de Young
steps.detail: Book a timed-entry morning slot for the Pharaohs blockbuster at the de Young ($40pp) — 130 objects, 3,000 years of history, and the US debut of objects from the newly excavated Golden City. Take your time.

steps.title: Lunch at Cotogna, North Beach
steps.detail: Drive or Lyft to Cotogna in North Beach for wood-fired Italian — handmade pasta, rotisserie meats, and the kind of unhurried lunch that makes an afternoon feel luxurious.

steps.title: BART to Berkeley
steps.detail: Take BART to Downtown Berkeley and wander the area — grab coffee, browse Moe's Books, decompress before the main event.

steps.title: Tori Amos at the Greek Theatre
steps.detail: Doors open at 7pm for Tori Amos with Bartees Strange at the Greek Theatre. Open-air, August stars, art rock perfection. This is the one.

solo.title: Bike, Block Party & Bay
solo.tagline: The last Friday of August belongs to you and your wheels.

steps.title: Visitacion Valley Night Market
steps.detail: Head down to Leland Avenue for the inaugural Visitacion Valley Night Market — food vendors, live music, street dancing, and a genuinely warm neighborhood crowd. First ever edition means you're part of history.

steps.title: SF Critical Mass — Embarcadero Plaza
steps.detail: Roll to Embarcadero Plaza and join Critical Mass — hundreds of cyclists, no route announced in advance, pure collective joy. Bring your bike or rent one nearby. This is quintessential SF.

steps.title: Wander & Wind Down
steps.detail: After the ride disperses, follow whoever seems fun to a bar or just cruise home on a quiet bike lane feeling very alive. No plan needed.

solo.title: Museum Morning, Comedy Night
solo.tagline: Brainy afternoon, funny evening — a complete solo Saturday.

steps.title: Lala Rukh: Subh-e-Umeed — Asian Art Museum
steps.detail: Spend the morning with Lala Rukh's sonic archive exhibition at the Asian Art Museum — headphones, birdsong, a morning in Lahore frozen in time. One of the most quietly powerful shows in SF right now.

steps.title: Hayes Valley Lunch
steps.detail: Walk to Hayes Valley for lunch — grab a seat somewhere with outdoor tables and people-watch with zero agenda. This is the solo move.

steps.title: Derrick Stroup at Punch Line SF
steps.detail: Solo comedy is criminally underrated — Punch Line is intimate, the seating is communal, and laughing next to strangers is its own kind of connection. From $35, multiple shows to choose from.

solo.title: Pharaohs & Symphonic Marvel
solo.tagline: Ancient history in the afternoon, cinematic orchestra at night — a Thursday for the books.

steps.title: Treasures of the Pharaohs — de Young
steps.detail: Book your timed entry ($40) and give yourself at least two hours with the Pharaohs exhibition in Golden Gate Park. The US debut objects from the Golden City are genuinely remarkable.

steps.title: Lunch at Tartine Manufactory
steps.detail: Walk or Lyft to Tartine Manufactory for a slow lunch — the bread alone is worth the trip and Thursday afternoon seating is more relaxed than weekends.

steps.title: Pre-Show Drink at Ordinaire — Hayes Valley
steps.detail: Natural wine, zero attitude, and a smart rotating list at Ordinaire — perfectly positioned near Davies Symphony Hall for a 6pm glass before the show.

steps.title: SF Symphony: Infinity Saga Concert Experience
steps.detail: Settle into Davies Symphony Hall for the SF Symphony performing the full Marvel Cinematic Universe score live. Acoustics of a great concert hall, music you already love — it genuinely works.

birthday.title: Golden Gate Park Birthday Tour
birthday.tagline: Your city, your park, your celebration — all for free.

steps.title: KOHO BonPop Bon Odori Festival
steps.detail: Start the birthday at the Bon Odori festival in the SF Botanical Gardens — free for SF residents, great music, traditional dancing, and a fountain plaza setting that feels genuinely festive. Fifth annual and still feels special.

steps.title: Golden Gate Park Wander
steps.detail: Walk the park as the afternoon light goes golden — the Conservatory of Flowers, Stow Lake, wherever feels right. No agenda, just the best park in the city doing its thing.

steps.title: Birthday Drinks at Zeitgeist
steps.detail: The Mission beer garden is the perfect birthday landing spot — big outdoor space, cold beers, cash only, bring whoever. No reservations, no fuss, just good company.

birthday.title: Pokémon XP + Night Market Birthday
birthday.tagline: Nerd out, eat everything, celebrate properly — peak long weekend birthday.

steps.title: Pokémon World Championships & XP — Moscone
steps.detail: If there was ever a birthday activity designed for the person who has a Pokémon preference, it's the World Championships weekend at Moscone. Pop-up Pokémon Center store, panels, and world-class competitive play all weekend.

steps.title: JouJou Birthday Lunch
steps.detail: Walk from Moscone to JouJou at 65 Division St for a celebratory seafood lunch — shellfish tower, Champagne, curved banquettes. This is the birthday table. Make a reservation ahead of time.

steps.title: Wax + DJ Hoppa at The Independent
steps.detail: Close the birthday Friday night with four hip-hop acts at The Independent — from $23, doors at 9pm, and the energy of a real music crowd to close out the celebration right.

birthday.title: Greek Theatre Birthday Night
birthday.tagline: Tori Amos under the stars — the most memorable birthday show of the summer.

steps.title: Birthday Brunch at Cotogna
steps.detail: Start with a long, celebratory Italian lunch at Cotogna in North Beach — wood-fired everything, natural wine, unhurried. The kind of birthday meal that people still talk about at dinner.

steps.title: SFMOMA Afternoon
steps.detail: Walk through SFMOMA's current highlights — the Graciela Iturbide retrospective and the Fisher Collection rehanging are both genuinely worth your time and feel appropriately celebratory.

steps.title: BART to Berkeley, Pre-Show Stroll
steps.detail: Head to Downtown Berkeley early, grab coffee or a cocktail, walk around before doors open at 7pm. Berkeley in August evenings is underrated.

steps.title: Tori Amos at the Greek Theatre
steps.detail: Tori Amos, Bartees Strange, open-air Greek Theatre, late August stars. This is the birthday concert memory. Go.

friends.title: Critical Mass Crew Ride
friends.tagline: The whole group, no plan, the whole city — classic SF Friday.

steps.title: Union Square Dances — Warm-Up
steps.detail: Meet at Union Square Park for the free outdoor dance party from 5–8pm. Rotating styles, outdoor energy, and an easy gathering point to get everyone in one place before the main event.

steps.title: SF Critical Mass — Embarcadero Plaza
steps.detail: Walk or ride to Embarcadero Plaza and join the Critical Mass mass bike ride — rent bikes nearby if needed. No route announced, just follow the crowd through the city together. Pure SF joy.

steps.title: Post-Ride Bar Crawl — Wherever It Goes
steps.detail: Let the group decide after the ride disperses. The Mission, SOMA, the Castro — Thursday night energy means plenty of options. No reservations, no plan, that's the point.

friends.title: Giants Double + Night Out
friends.tagline: Doubleheader baseball then Divisadero for the night — the perfect Saturday crew move.

steps.title: Giants vs. Diamondbacks Doubleheader — Oracle Park
steps.detail: Saturday doubleheader means two full games — stock up on garlic fries, rotate seating between games, make it a real baseball afternoon. Oracle Park with a crew is one of SF's best group activities.

steps.title: Post-Game Beers at Zeitgeist
steps.detail: BART or Lyft from the ballpark to Zeitgeist in the Mission — massive beer garden, cash only, cold pitchers. The perfect post-game decompression spot.

steps.title: Brenn! at The Independent
steps.detail: Walk up Divisadero from the Mission to The Independent for Brenn! at 9pm — emerging indie-pop in a great mid-sized venue. A natural Saturday night cap that doesn't require a ton of planning.

friends.title: Nas & The Roots + JouJou Dinner
friends.tagline: The biggest hip-hop show of the weekend plus the hottest new restaurant — go big.

steps.title: Mess Hall Food Hall Pre-Game — The Presidio
steps.detail: Start with a casual late lunch at the new Mess Hall Food Hall in the Presidio — seafood, Korean, burgers, sandwiches, a full bar. Easy group logistics, great food, beautiful Presidio setting.

steps.title: JouJou Dinner Reservation — SoMa
steps.detail: Book ahead for JouJou at 65 Division St — shellfish towers, oysters, Champagne, the full celebratory French seafood experience from the Lazy Bear team. This is the dinner.

steps.title: Nas & The Roots at Shoreline Amphitheatre
steps.detail: Head to Mountain View for 'A Great Night in Hip Hop' featuring Nas and The Roots at Shoreline. Book an Uber from the city — show starts at 7pm and this is genuinely one of the biggest live music events of the holiday weekend.

parents.title: Golden Gate Park Sunday
parents.tagline: The park does the work — all you have to do is show up.

steps.title: Golden Gate Park Morning Walk
steps.detail: Start with a morning stroll through Golden Gate Park — the Conservatory of Flowers, the Bison Paddock, the Dutch Windmill. No tickets, no agenda, beautiful.

steps.title: KOHO BonPop Bon Odori Festival
steps.detail: The Bon Odori festival takes over the SF Botanical Gardens Fountain Plaza from 2–6pm — free for SF residents, family-friendly, live music and traditional dancing in a gorgeous garden setting. A genuinely lovely Sunday afternoon with your folks.

steps.title: Sunset at Ocean Beach
steps.detail: Walk or drive the short distance to Ocean Beach for the sunset. Bring layers. Watch the waves. This is the SF moment parents always want.

parents.title: Pharaohs & Ferry Building
parents.tagline: World-class museum, iconic market lunch — a parent-approved San Francisco classic.

steps.title: Treasures of the Pharaohs — de Young Museum
steps.detail: Book timed entry ($40pp) for the Pharaohs exhibition in Golden Gate Park — 130 objects spanning 3,000 years, and your parents will be genuinely wowed. Allow at least two hours.

steps.title: Ferry Building Lunch
steps.detail: Walk or drive to the Ferry Building for lunch — Hog Island oysters, Acme bread, Cowgirl Creamery cheese, whatever catches their eye. The setting on the Embarcadero is hard to beat.

steps.title: Exploratorium — Life in Space
steps.detail: End the afternoon at the Exploratorium's Life in Space exhibition at Pier 15 — hands-on, fascinating, and the kind of thing parents and kids actually enjoy together. Closes the day on a high.

parents.title: Symphony Marvel Night + Cotogna Dinner
parents.tagline: World-class Italian dinner, world-class orchestra — a Thursday your parents will talk about.

steps.title: Dinner at Cotogna — North Beach
steps.detail: Bring your parents to Cotogna for a proper celebratory Italian dinner — wood-fired pasta, rotisserie meats, warm neighborhood room. Make the reservation well ahead and order the whole menu.

steps.title: Walk to Davies Symphony Hall
steps.detail: Stroll from North Beach to Van Ness area or grab a quick Lyft — Davies Symphony Hall is beautiful before a show and worth arriving a few minutes early to look around.

steps.title: SF Symphony: Marvel Infinity Saga Concert Experience
steps.detail: The full MCU score performed live by the SF Symphony conducted by Anthony Parnther at Davies. Even non-classical parents will be moved by this — the acoustics in that hall are extraordinary and the music is completely familiar. A perfect night.
